title: Using Non-Lipschitz Signum-based Functions for Distributed Optimization and Machine Learning: Trade-off Between Con-vergence Rate and Optimality Gap
summary: In recent years, the prevalence of large-scale data-sets and the demand for sophisti-cated learning models have necessitated the development of efficient distributed ma-chine learning (ML) solutions. Convergence speed is a critical factor influencing the practicality and effectiveness of these distributed frameworks. Recently, non-Lipschitz continuous optimization algorithms have been proposed to improve the slow conver-gence rate of the existing linear solutions.
